# `silk/time/mark`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Readings of a monotonic clock: the [`Mark`](#Mark) type.

## When to use

Use a [`Mark`](#Mark) to measure how long something takes and to hold a deadline. A mark comes from a
clock that never goes back, such as `silk.system.monotonic_clock`. For a date and time that
you show, store, or send, use `silk.time.instant`.

## Details

A mark is a point on the timeline of one clock. The origin of that timeline is not specified,
so a mark has no date. It has a meaning only next to another mark of the same clock: the later
one minus the earlier one is the [`Duration`](silk.time.duration.Duration) between them, and a
mark plus a span is a deadline. Marks are ordered, so `&now >= &deadline` tests a deadline.

## Gotchas

The compiler cannot stop a program from comparing marks of two different clocks. The result of
such a comparison has no meaning.

## Examples

### Compute a deadline and the time left

```silk
import silk.time.duration { Duration }
import silk.time.mark { Mark }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // A test clock can make marks from plain numbers. A real clock returns them from `now`.
  let start = Mark.make(100, 0)
  let deadline = start + Duration.fromMilliseconds(1500)
  let now = Mark.make(101, 0)
  if &now >= &deadline {
    return 1
  }
  if &(deadline - now) != &Duration.fromMilliseconds(500) {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `Mark`

```silk
pub struct Mark
```

A reading of a monotonic clock, with nanosecond precision.

### Details

A mark is the time since the origin of its clock, which is not specified and can be before or
after the start of the program. `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare marks.
`mark + span` and `mark - span` return a mark, and `later - earlier` returns the span between
two marks. They trap when the result is outside the range, which is the range of a
[`Duration`](silk.time.duration.Duration).

<a id="Mark.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(seconds: i64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Mark
```

Returns the mark `seconds` seconds plus `nanoseconds` nanoseconds after the origin of a clock.

#### When to use

A clock provider calls it to build the marks that it returns, and a test calls it for fixed
marks. Other code gets marks from a clock.

#### Details

Whole seconds in `nanoseconds` move into the seconds, and both parts can be negative. A total
outside the `i64` seconds range traps.


the range.

<a id="Mark.impl.since"></a>

### Method `since`

```silk
pub fn since(self: Self, earlier: Mark) -> Duration
```

Returns the span from `earlier` to this mark. It is negative when `earlier` is later.

#### Gotchas

Both marks must come from the same clock. A span outside the `Duration` range traps.

<a id="Mark.impl.until"></a>

### Method `until`

```silk
pub fn until(self: Self, later: Mark) -> Duration
```

Returns the span from this mark to `later`. It is negative when `later` is earlier.

#### Gotchas

Both marks must come from the same clock. A span outside the `Duration` range traps.
